scenes.narration: One gift tore a family apart. Israel loved his son Joseph more than all his other children, because Joseph was the son of his old age. And he gave him something none of the others had: “a coat of many colours.”
scenes.image_prompt: {JOSEPH} holding up a beautiful new coat of many colours with delight, smiling, inside a tent, warm lamp light, his elderly father softly blurred in the background

scenes.narration: His brothers saw it. Their father loved Joseph more than any of them. And they hated him for it, so much that they could not speak a peaceful word to him.
scenes.image_prompt: close-up of {BROTHERS} faces scowling with jealousy, side-eyeing, shepherd's field behind them, harsh afternoon light

scenes.narration: Then Joseph had a dream, and he told his brothers. They were binding sheaves of grain in the field, he said, when his sheaf rose and stood upright, and all their sheaves gathered around it and bowed down to it. And they hated him even more.
scenes.image_prompt: {JOSEPH} sleeping peacefully on a woven mat under a starry night sky, above him a glowing dreamlike vision of golden wheat sheaves bowing in a circle, dreamy light

scenes.narration: Later, when Joseph came to his brothers, they seized him. They stripped him of his coat, the coat of many colours. Then they threw him into a pit. The pit was empty. There was no water in it.
scenes.image_prompt: view from above looking down into a deep dry stone pit in the desert, {JOSEPH_STRIPPED} alone at the bottom looking up, a rope hanging down, dramatic dusk light
